body:
## Summary

Rhythm's current memory model supports basic source/path metadata but not the richer provenance and lifecycle semantics recently assumed by a manually edited consolidation prompt.

Current memory rows expose `source`, `sourceId`, tags, owner, and timestamps. There is no supported immutable source list, actor/generated-by field, verification history, stale-after state, deprecation state, change log, or rollback target. The MCP surface likewise has no `rhythm_verify_memory` tool.

Design and implement these capabilities deliberately rather than encoding nonexistent behavior in prompts.

## Likely files

- memory model/frontmatter schema
- `apps/api_server/src/repositories/agent_memory_repository.ts`
- `apps/api_server/src/services/memoryVaultWriteService.ts`
- `apps/api_server/src/services/memoryVaultSyncService.ts`
- `apps/api_server/src/controllers/agentMemoryController.ts`
- `apps/mcp_server/src/tools/agentMemory.ts`
- desktop Memory/Brain UI files
- SQLite migrations and schema/backfill tests

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A design decision defines canonical provenance fields, actor identity, source references, lifecycle states, and rollback semantics before implementation.
- [ ] Provenance survives vault write, reindex, update, and retrieval.
- [ ] Verification/deprecation is non-destructive and auditable.
- [ ] Every change records actor, timestamp, prior state or rollback target, and source context.
- [ ] Staleness is represented without silently deleting memories.
- [ ] MCP tool schemas and descriptions match the actual API contract.
- [ ] Existing vault notes and index rows migrate additively with safe defaults.
- [ ] UI distinguishes active, stale, deprecated, and unverifiable memories without hiding provenance.

## Required validation

- Migration and backfill tests.
- Vault round-trip tests.
- MCP schema/behavior tests.
- Immutable change-history and rollback tests.
- Desktop rendering/state tests.
- Env-gated live behavioral test through the real API/MCP surface.
- GitNexus impact analysis before editing and `detect_changes()` before commit.

## Safety / out of scope

- No destructive column drops or bulk deletion.
- Do not invent provenance for legacy rows; represent it as unknown/unverified.
- Do not treat deprecation as deletion.
- Any production/Postgres work requires explicit confirmation because current memory is documented as local-only.

## Dependencies

- Complete the supported Memory Consolidation prompt repair first so prompts do not depend on this future design.
title: Design memory provenance and lifecycle support
